reviewed_by: Gemini Pro blind reviewer, batch G3-NA-Q3-Harden (mat_g3_na_q3_6), 2026-08-18

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The items directly assess explaining how to generate compound number patterns containing both repeating and increasing/decreasing components. Questions such as 'This pattern follows a rule: 24, 24, 34, 34, 44, ... Each group of numbers repeats, then the next group changes by the same amount. What number is added or subtracted from one group to the next?' (seed 42) explicitly prompt the student to formulate and identify the generative transformation between successive repeating periods.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The sample set comprehensively covers both repeating-increasing and repeating-decreasing patterns across varied step sizes. Increasing sequences are well represented (e.g. seed 42 adding 10 in 'This pattern follows a rule: 24, 24, 34, 34, 44, ... Each group of numbers repeats, then the next group changes by the same amount. What number is added or subtracted from one group to the next?' and seed 502 adding 20 in 'This pattern follows a rule: 43, 47, 41, 63, 67, 61, 83, 87, ... Each group of numbers repeats, then the next group changes by the same amount. What number is added or subtracted from one group to the next?'), as are decreasing sequences (e.g. seed 44 subtracting 10 in 'This pattern follows a rule: 44, 45, 41, 34, 35, 31, 24, 25, ... Each group of numbers repeats, then the next group changes by the same amount. What number is added or subtracted from one group to the next?' and seed 45 subtracting 100 in 'This pattern follows a rule: 212, 215, 216, 112, 115, 116, 12, 15, ... Each group of numbers repeats, then the next group changes by the same amount. What number is added or subtracted from one group to the next?').

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The cognitive demand is well-tuned for Grade 3 Quarter 3 students. The scaffolding statement ('Each group of numbers repeats, then the next group changes by the same amount') clarifies the structure of the pattern without solving it for the student, as demonstrated in 'This pattern follows a rule: 224, 229, 124, 129, 24, ... Each group of numbers repeats, then the next group changes by the same amount. What number is added or subtracted from one group to the next?' (seed 46). Period lengths of 2 and 3 items keep working memory load manageable.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The packet exercises both multiple choice and cloze/fill-in formats while systematically varying the internal group size (2 items in seed 43 'This pattern follows a rule: 33, 38, 83, 88, 133, ... Each group of numbers repeats, then the next group changes by the same amount. What number is added or subtracted from one group to the next?'; 3 items in seed 500 'This pattern follows a rule: 237, 234, 232, 137, 134, 132, 37, 34, ... Each group of numbers repeats, then the next group changes by the same amount. What number is added or subtracted from one group to the next?') and step differences (10, 20, 50, 100).

competency_alignment.rationale: The items remain strictly within the boundaries of the MATATAG learning competency. In items like 'This pattern follows a rule: 136, 136, 139, 86, 86, 89, 36, 36, ... Each group of numbers repeats, then the next group changes by the same amount. What number is added or subtracted from one group to the next?' (seed 501), the task targets the generative mechanism of repeating and decreasing components without introducing out-of-scope arithmetic or algebraic notations.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Number domains and step values are completely appropriate for Grade 3 arithmetic. Starting terms remain within 2-digit to low 3-digit ranges (e.g. seed 50 'This pattern follows a rule: 114, 118, 116, 64, 68, 66, 14, 18, ... Each group of numbers repeats, then the next group changes by the same amount. What number is added or subtracted from one group to the next?' starting at 114 and descending by 50 to 14), and differences align with standard skip-counting intervals (10, 20, 50, 100).
